title: Repeated recursion in 0-1 knapsack
summary: In a dedicated three-item example with capacity 30, two different decision paths reach dp[1, 10]. Each expands its subtree once, so it is expanded twice in total.
context: In 0-1 knapsack, each item may be chosen at most once. Note that this figure uses a separate 3-item example distinct from the earlier figure and the main driver code: knapsack capacity cap = 30, and the 3 items have weights 10, 20, 20 and values 60, 110, 120 (see the table). State dp[i, c] denotes the maximum value obtainable from the first i items with remaining capacity c; the table header in the drawing writes wgt[i] and val[i] (with item IDs i starting at 1), whereas the code in the text indexes the arrays at i - 1.

When the current item fits, compare dp[i-1, c] (excluding it) with dp[i-1, c-wgt[i-1]] + val[i-1] (including it) and take the larger value; when it does not fit, take only the exclude branch. With no items left (i = 0) or remaining capacity 0 (c = 0), return 0.
description: Recursion starts at the root dp[3, 30] and makes decisions in order for item 3 (pineapple, weight 20, value 120), item 2 (watermelon, weight 20, value 110), and item 1 (apple, weight 10, value 60). Because item 2 and item 3 both have weight 20, taking either "exclude item 3, then include item 2" (dp[3, 30] → dp[2, 30] → dp[1, 10]) or "include item 3, then exclude item 2" (dp[3, 30] → dp[2, 10] → dp[1, 10]) subtracts weight 20, leaves capacity 10, and leaves only item 1 to consider, so the two distinct paths converge on the same subproblem dp[1, 10].

Brute-force search does not record previously solved subproblems, so upon encountering the two occurrences of dp[1, 10], it expands each one downward separately, comparing dp[0, 10] (excluding item 1) with dp[0, 0] + 60 (including item 1) both times; thus the same subproblem dp[1, 10] is expanded twice in full, making the second expansion redundant.

At the right child dp[2, 10], the remaining capacity is 10 while item 2 has weight 20, exceeding the remaining capacity. The node dp[1, -10] drawn in the figure is labeled "Prune: item weight > knapsack capacity" solely to illustrate the excluded overweight branch; the code in the text checks whether the item weight exceeds the remaining capacity before recursing, calling only the exclude branch dp[1, 10] when overweight rather than making a call with negative capacity.

The two tables below list the dedicated input items and the complete recursion tree shown in the figure; using the decision path from the root as the row header distinguishes multiple occurrences of the same state.

From the input data, choosing item 1 and item 3 gives total weight 10 + 20 = 30 and maximum value 60 + 120 = 180; the value 180 is not written directly on the tree nodes.
